newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Flagging SAfrica gold output seen under 495 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Flagging SAfrica gold output seen under 495 tonnes.

text.p: The South African gold mining industry is set to finish a difficult year with ouput just 490-495 tonnes of the precious metal, down from the 500 tonnes previously hoped for, the Chamber of Mines said on Tuesday.
It promises to be the worst year for gold production since 1956 with output half that produced in 1970 and some six percent down on last year's 522.4 tonnes.

"The one thing is certain, we can forget about 500 tonnes. We're probably looking at a total of between 490 and 495 tonnes," Dan Pollnow, gold marketing consultant at the mine employers' body, told Reuters.

The Chamber released November gold output figures on Tuesday showing a miniscule improvement in November production to 41.68 tonnes compared to October's 41.09 tonnes. But it is the year-to-date numbers which hold the reality of the situation.
"A month taken in isolation doesn't mean all that much. If we look at the cumulative or the year to date we're down about six percent," Pollnow said.
The industry's gold output for 1996 to date is 450.6 tonnes compared to 1995's 478.0 tonnes -- a 5.7 percent decline.

Still, in line with many independent analysts, the Chamber's Pollnow said that this could be the bottom of the slide for South Africa's beleaguered and ageing gold mining industry, although no rapid improvement was on the cards.

"It would seem as though the slide which we've been seeing since the beginning of 1994 has slowed considerably. We are probably at the bottom. I don't know if we're going to pick up but I don't think we're going to see the decrease we've seen this year," Pollnow said.
Looking back over a year which suffered declining ore grade, labour unrest and criminal violence, Pollnow said:

"It has been a very difficult year. Grades have continued to decrease, there have been technical difficulties, industrial relations haven't been all that good and managements have been under huge pressure."
Labour unrest was familiar with numerous strikes at various mines. Furthermore, criminal violence, ethnically-triggered, took its toll on platinum mines and certain gold mines too.
But Pollnow remained optimistic about the future, citing the several major expansion projects underway and in the pipeline.
"The industry has learnt a lot over the year and I am reasonably confident in saying that we've probably seen the worst of it."
